quarterly_data.signal: Planet 10-K (fiscal year ended January 31, 2026): revenue $307.7 million, up 26%, primarily driven by a $64.0 million increase in the defense and intelligence vertical (defense and intelligence $180,232 thousand, civil government $71,910 thousand, commercial $55,585 thousand); revenue from Japan was $38.0 million and from Ukraine $35.9 million; two customers accounted for 13% and 12% of revenue and one customer for 33% of accounts receivable; gross margin 56% (non-GAAP 59%), adjusted EBITDA $15,495 thousand and net cash from operations $134,362 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $307.7 million (26%); defense and intelligence $180,232 thousand; customers 13% and 12%; adjusted EBITDA $15,495 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Planet 10-K: backlog was $900,427 thousand (remaining performance obligations $852.4 million, approximately 34% within the next 12 months; backlog approximately 37% within 12 months); net dollar retention rate 116% (118% including winbacks), primarily due to large defense and intelligence contract expansions; recurring ACV 98%; capital expenditures were 26% of revenue ($81.5 million), mainly capitalized labor and material for the next-generation high resolution Pelican satellites and medium resolution satellites.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog $900,427 thousand; RPO $852.4 million; NDR 116%; capex $81.5 million (26% of revenue)

quarterly_data.signal: Planet 10-K: in December 2025 Planet entered a multi-year low 9-figure commercial agreement with the Swedish Armed Forces to build and operate a constellation of Pelican high resolution satellites owned by SwAF, with licensing rights to certain imagery from the Pelicans for Planet's customers; on November 14, 2025 Planet acquired Bedrock's multi-modal geospatial AI technology business; as a NASA Communication Services Project subcontractor to two satellite communications providers, Planet is to receive aggregate funding of $40.5 million ($30.4 million received); all satellite manufacturing, testing and R&D occurs at the approximately 71,280 square foot San Francisco headquarters.
quarterly_data.figure: low 9-figure SwAF agreement; NASA CSP funding $40.5 million; 71,280 square feet
